# パランティアの衝撃：データとAIを繋ぐ「オントロジー」戦略

> A structural analysis by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist,
> explaining Palantir Foundry's "Ontology" — not as an IT technology, but as
> an operational layer that models the world as nouns (objects, properties,
> links) and verbs (actions, functions, dynamic security), enabling AI to
> act safely on real-world operations through a branch-and-review
> governance process. As stated in the book: "The paradigm shift Palantir
> brings — the 'Ontology' — is a fundamental break from siloed data:
> a shift from data you only look at, to data that directly drives the
> business."

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/the-palantir-impact_jp.md): Part I〜III・全6章・参考文献収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/the-palantir-impact_en.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book states Palantir's Ontology unifies "semantics" (object types,
  properties, link types — the noun world) and "kinetics" (actions,
  functions, dynamic security — the verb world) into a single backend,
  built on five core services: OMS, Object databases, OSS, Actions, and
  Funnel
- The book states that changes to the Ontology follow a branch-and-review
  lifecycle ("Ontology Proposals"): changes are made on a branch, reviewed
  and approved, then merged into the main environment — modeled explicitly
  on the pull-request pattern from software engineering
- The book states Palantir's "AI FDE" (AI-powered forward deployed
  engineer) converts natural-language requests into Foundry operations,
  but strictly respects the user's existing permissions and must submit a
  branch proposal for human review before any change is merged
- The book cites the Airbus case: integrating data on ~5 million parts of
  the A350 onto the Ontology accelerated aircraft delivery by 33%, and
  100+ airlines now use the resulting "Skywise" platform to process
  telemetry from up to 20,000 sensors per aircraft
- The book cites the SOMPO Holdings case: Palantir was adopted as the core
  of SOMPO's "Real Data Platform," with 8,000+ employees in Japan using it
  for insurance claims triage and fraud detection
- The book cites Fujitsu and Palantir Japan's December 2023 press release
  expanding their global partnership
- The book proposes a 5-month implementation roadmap: (1) understanding
  backend structure and permissions, (2) minimal modeling and branch
  operations, (3) data pipeline verification, (4) audit and governance
  design, (5) integration with AI and external applications via OSDK
